newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW-German February M3 money supply data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-German February M3 money supply data.

text.p: Following are reactions from economists to publication by the Bundesbank of February M3 money supply growth data showing a 9.1 percent annualised rise compared to 11.7 percent in January.

ADOLF ROSENSTOCK, IBJ Frankfurt: (These figures) seem to show that the economy is coming back to life. It's just lower than expected because capital formation was lower, but I doubt that this will continue."
JEREMY HAWKINS, BANK OF AMERICA: "The overall figure looks soft but the breakdown seems to indicate otherwise."

"This is good news, the economy is not that strong at the moment. I think the Bundesbank will reach its target for M3 for year". (The central bank has set a target of between 3.5 and 6.5 percent M3 money supply growth in 1997).

KAREN KRICKS-BRUNNLIEB, TRINKHAUS CAPITAL MANAGEMENT: "During the course of February the pace of money stock expansion slowed slightly more than expected...On the other side, however, the recent weakness of the German bond market should have depressed money capital formation in March. Therefore, an entry into the target corridor should not be expected before the summer, at earliest.
Against this background, the Bundesbank has definitely no reason to lower its interest rates...The Bundesbank should stick to the fixed rate repo of three percent for the foreseeable future.
